text:
pagerbot: URGENT: PagerDuty alert triggered for inference-gateway (us-west1) — sustained 5xx error rate > 6% over last 1m (metric: http.responses.5xx_rate). Service: inference-gateway-prod, route: /v1/generate. PD incident: #PD-79321. Paging SRE.

sre-oncall: @pagerbot ack. I'm oncall — digging in. Starting with LB and canary checks. ETA 5m.

eng-raj: FYI I deployed a small canary of model-quant-v2 to us-west1 ~12m ago (canary weight 5%). No other infra changes.

infra-megan: On it too — checking autoscaler and healthcheck failures. Noting increased backend 502s on nodes behind nw-igw-usw1.

sre-oncall: quick check: curl -I https://gateway-usw1.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "x-api-key: REDACTED"  (paste)

sre-oncall: ```
HTTP/2 502
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream response invalid"}
```

eng-raj: Seeing similar in app logs. Example from svc-inference (pod inference-abc-123):
```
2026-03-01T03:12:10Z ERROR kvcache: failed to stream kv: connection reset by peer
2026-03-01T03:12:11Z WARN http: upstream 10.4.5.12:8080 returned 502
```

infra-megan: Autoscaler shows spike in CPU and instance churn. Some pods failing readiness and re-creating. Could be memory regression in new runtime or quantized model OOM.

deploybot: Deploy log: model-quant-v2 canary rollout started by @eng-raj at 2026-03-01T03:00Z. 5% traffic. No automatic rollback triggered.

sre-oncall: Action plan: 1) Pause canary traffic -> shift to previous variant 2) Temporarily divert traffic to us-east1 fallback 3) Scale up pod replicas in usw1 to soak 4) Collect heap/dmesg from failing pods. Starting step 1 now.

eng-raj: Agreed. Pausing canary and rolling back weight to model-quant-v1. I'll trigger in 30s.

sre-oncall: @eng-raj confirmed rollback requested.

deploybot: Canary update: model-quant-v2 weight set to 0%. Rolling back to model-quant-v1 for routing.

sre-oncall: quick health after rollback: curl returns 200 on /healthz from gateway edges but /v1/generate still seeing intermittent 502s from certain backends. Collecting traces now.

infra-megan: Noting one node with repeated OOMKilled events: node-id: gke-usw1-n3. Pulling kernel logs.

sre-oncall: PD note: acknowledged by sre-oncall at 1809123462. If no improvement in 10m we'll escalate to Eng Lead.

cs-ash: Any ETA on customer impact? Are there customer-facing errors? I can open a status page if needed.

sre-oncall: Early check: ~3% of requests across US users hit 5xx, concentrated to a handful of customers using long-context embeddings + streaming. Will flag CS if >5% or >2 enterprise customers affected.

eng-raj: I can push a patch with a kv-cache retry guard (limit concurrent read threads) but that will take ~20m to test. Prefer rollback first (done).

sre-oncall: After rollback, 5xx dropped to ~1.6% in the last 2m (from 6.2%). Trending down. Keeping traffic routed to v1. Will continue to monitor for 15m.

infra-megan: Node with OOM restarted; kube events show image memory use spike before crash. Placing node in cordon to stop new pods until we investigate.

sre-oncall: cordon complete. Starting graceful reschedule. Adding temporary pod anti-affinity to avoid packing failing instance.

pagerbot: PD update: Incident PD-79321 status updated — Acknowledged by sre-oncall. Escalation timer paused. (link to PD)

sre-oncall: Summary so far for timeline: 03:00 canary deploy model-quant-v2 -> 03:10 spike in 5xx -> pager fired 03:15 -> rollback initiated 03:22 -> 5xx rate falling 03:24. Root cause suspected: increased memory pressure / inefficient kv-cache behavior with quantized model under high concurrency.

eng-raj: Will open a follow-up ticket referencing pod logs and heap dumps: INF-2478. I'll also run a local stress test with quant-v2 and KV thread limits.

cs-ash: Notifying affected customers proactively: sending a brief noting degraded inference performance and partial errors while we investigate. Will link to incident PD-79321 and status page.

sre-oncall: Closing note: keeping the incident on watch for 30m. If metrics remain stable we'll resolve. Thanks team :thumbsup:

pagerbot: PD-79321 resolved by sre-oncall at 1809123620 (monitoring).
